events.title: Abraham makes his servant swear to find Isaac a wife
events.narrative_summary: Abraham, old and blessed in everything, has his senior servant swear by the God of heaven not to take a Canaanite wife for Isaac but to go to his own land and kindred. The servant asks if he should take Isaac there; Abraham refuses, promises that God's angel will go before him, and releases him from the oath if the woman will not come.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No date is given beyond 'Abraham was old' (v.1). The scene is set after Sarah's burial (Gen 23) and before Isaac's marriage at forty (Gen 25:20). Radak on v.67 says Sarah had been dead three years when Isaac took Rebekah. The journey out (27 d), the stay (1 night) and the journey back (31 d) take about 2.5 months, so the oath falls about 2.75 years after the burial, margin 6 months. Duration about an hour for the speeches.
events.ancient_year_marker: Abraham was old, well advanced in days

events.title: The servant takes ten camels to Nahor's city
events.narrative_summary: The servant takes ten of his master's camels and goods of every kind and sets out for Aram-Naharaim, to the city of Nahor.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The text gives no duration. Hebron to Haran by road is about 869 km; `urim travel --mode donkey` gives 4 km/h, about 32 km a day, elapsed about 27 days. Camels are not a listed mode, so donkey pace is used. Margin 5 days for the route and the identification of Nahor's city. Starts the moment the oath ends.

events.title: The servant kneels his camels at the well outside the city
events.narrative_summary: Outside the city, by the well, the servant makes his camels kneel at evening, the time when the women go out to draw water.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: v.11 says 'at the time of evening, the time of the going out of the women who draw water'. This is the late afternoon draw before dark, set at BEIN_HAARBAYIM (17:30), and the start snaps to the first such time after the journey ends. Margin 30 minutes. Duration is the time to halt and unload.
events.ancient_diurnal_marker: At the time of evening, the time the women go out to draw water

events.title: The servant prays for a sign at the well
events.narrative_summary: The servant asks the God of Abraham to grant him success that day, and names the sign: the girl who answers his request for a drink by offering to water his camels too will be the one appointed for Isaac.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Begins when the halt ends, at the same evening. A prayer of three verses takes a few minutes; margin 5 minutes.

events.title: Rebekah comes to the well and waters the servant and his camels
events.narrative_summary: Before the servant has finished speaking, Rebekah, Bethuel's daughter, comes out with her jar. She fills it, gives the servant a drink and then draws water for all his camels while he watches in silence to learn whether the LORD has prospered his journey.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: v.15 'before he had finished speaking' puts her arrival inside the prayer, so the event is anchored on the prayer's START with an offset of 4 minutes (the prayer lasts about 4, so she arrives as it ends; the margin covers 'before he had finished'). Watering ten camels from a well by jar takes about an hour (my estimate). Margin 5 minutes.

events.title: The servant gives Rebekah gold and asks about her family
events.narrative_summary: When the camels have finished drinking, the servant gives Rebekah a gold ring and two gold bracelets and asks whose daughter she is and whether there is room to lodge. She names her father Bethuel and offers straw, fodder and room.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows at once, 'as the camels had finished drinking' (v.22). A short exchange, about ten minutes.
events.ancient_diurnal_marker: When the camels had finished drinking

events.title: The servant bows and blesses the LORD for his guidance
events.narrative_summary: The man bows down and worships the LORD, blessing the God of Abraham who has not abandoned his steadfast love and has led him to his master's kinsmen.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows Rebekah's answer at once, at the well. It overlaps the start of her run home (v.28) and is anchored on the same point; about five minutes.

events.title: Rebekah runs home and tells her mother's house
events.narrative_summary: Rebekah runs to her mother's house and tells them what has happened.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: She leaves as the exchange ends (v.28). The house is in the city, near the well, so about fifteen minutes with the telling.

events.title: Laban runs to the well and brings the servant home
events.narrative_summary: Laban sees the ring and bracelets on his sister and hears her account, then runs out to the man at the well and invites him in. He unloads the camels, gives them straw and fodder, and brings water to wash the feet of the servant and his men.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows Rebekah's report (vv.29-30). Running, greeting, walking in and seeing to the camels and water takes about an hour, still the same evening; margin 15 minutes.

events.title: The servant refuses to eat until he has told his errand
events.narrative_summary: Food is set before him but the servant will not eat until he has spoken. He tells how Abraham was blessed, how Isaac was born to Sarah, the oath he swore, the prayer at the well, Rebekah's answering of it, and how he gave her the gifts, then asks for a plain answer.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows the welcome (v.33). The speech retells vv.2-27 and takes about half an hour; margin 15 minutes.

events.title: Laban and Bethuel say the matter comes from the LORD
events.narrative_summary: Laban and Bethuel answer that the matter has come from the LORD and that they cannot say bad or good; Rebekah is before him, to take and go and be the wife of his master's son, as the LORD has spoken.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Immediate answer to the speech; about ten minutes.

events.title: The servant worships and gives gifts to Rebekah and her family
events.narrative_summary: Hearing their answer, the servant bows to the ground before the LORD. He brings out silver and gold jewelry and garments for Rebekah and gives precious things to her brother and mother.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows the consent at once; about twenty minutes.

events.title: The servant and his men eat, drink and stay the night
events.narrative_summary: The servant and the men with him eat and drink and spend the night in Bethuel's house.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The meal follows the gifts; 'they lodged' (v.54) covers the night. The hours until the morning are not timed; four hours is an estimate for the meal and settling down, and the next event snaps to the morning. Margin 1 hour.

events.title: At daybreak the servant asks to be sent to his master
events.narrative_summary: When they rise in the morning the servant asks to be sent back to his master. Rebekah's brother and mother ask that she stay 'days or ten' first, but the servant begs them not to delay him since the LORD has prospered his way.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: v.54 'they rose up in the morning', BOKER (06:00), the first morning after the night event ends. Duration 30 minutes for the exchange. The request for 'days or ten' is only asked, not granted; see the reviewer note on Rashi and Radak.

events.title: Rebekah agrees to go with the man
events.narrative_summary: They decide to call the girl and ask her. They call Rebekah and ask whether she will go with this man, and she says, 'I will go.'
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows at once the same morning; about fifteen minutes.

events.title: Her family blesses Rebekah and sends her off with the servant
events.narrative_summary: They send Rebekah with her nurse, the servant and his men, and bless her that she become thousands of myriads and that her seed possess the gate of those who hate them. Rebekah and her maids mount the camels and follow the man.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The packing and farewell follow the consent; offset 1 hour (my estimate for the preparations), duration 1 hour, margin 1 hour. The same morning.

events.title: The servant takes Rebekah south to Canaan
events.narrative_summary: The servant takes Rebekah and goes his way, back toward his master's land.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No duration is given. Haran to Beer-lahai-roi is about 1015 km by road; `urim travel --mode donkey` gives about 32 km a day, elapsed about 31 days. Margin 5 days. Starts when the departure ends.

events.title: Isaac sees the camels coming and Rebekah veils herself
events.narrative_summary: Isaac, who had come from Beer-lahai-roi and lived in the Negeb, goes out into the field toward evening to meditate and sees camels coming. Rebekah sees him, gets down from her camel, asks the servant who the man is, and covers herself with her veil when she is told it is his master.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: v.63 'at the turning of evening' (Ibn Ezra: close to sunset; Radak: when people go out to walk). The first such time after the journey ends, BEIN_HAARBAYIM (17:30). The text gives only the hour, so margin 30 minutes.

events.title: Isaac marries Rebekah and is comforted after his mother's death
events.narrative_summary: The servant tells Isaac everything he has done. Isaac brings Rebekah into his mother Sarah's tent and takes her as his wife, and loves her, and is comforted after his mother's death.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows the meeting the same evening or soon after. The text names no hour; margin 1 day. Radak puts the marriage three years after Sarah died; see the reviewer note comparing it with Gen 25:20 (Isaac forty).

causal_edges.causal_explanation: Having sworn the oath at Abraham's command, the servant sets out for Nahor's city to find Isaac a wife (24:9-10).
Abraham's word that God would send his angel before the servant (24:7) is borne out when the servant is led to the girl at the well, as he confesses in 24:27.
Rebekah's 'I will go' (24:58) is why they send her off with the servant (24:59).
After meeting Rebekah and hearing the servant's report, Isaac takes her into Sarah's tent as his wife (24:66-67).
Laban runs to the man at the well after hearing Rebekah's account and seeing the jewelry on her (24:30).
When the servant presses to go, the family calls Rebekah to ask her own mind (24:57).
The servant asks for the girl who offers to water his camels (24:14), and Rebekah does exactly that (24:18-20).
The servant's account of the oath, the prayer and the sign leads Laban and Bethuel to say the matter is from the LORD (24:50).

aliases: jewels of silver and gold and garments
entities.etymology_meaning: 'Keli' means vessel or article; the list is silver articles, gold articles and clothing.
entities.summary_bio: Articles of silver and gold and garments that the servant gives Rebekah once her family consents. He also gives precious things to her brother and mother.

entities.etymology_meaning: 'Tsamid' means a bracelet or band; the pair weighs ten shekels of gold.
entities.summary_bio: Two gold bracelets, together weighing ten gold shekels, put on Rebekah's hands by the servant at the well.

entities.etymology_meaning: 'Nezem' is a ring worn in the nose or ear; the weight is a beka, about half a shekel.
entities.summary_bio: A gold ring of a beka's weight that the servant gives Rebekah at the well. Laban sees it on his sister's hands when he runs to the well.
Ten camels taken from Abraham's herds to carry the servant and his master's goods to Nahor's city. Rebekah draws water for all of them, which is the sign the servant asked for.

entities.etymology_meaning: 'Na'arah' means young woman or female attendant.
entities.summary_bio: The female attendants who ride with Rebekah on camels when she leaves her family's house to follow Abraham's servant.

aliases: the men who were with him
entities.summary_bio: The companions who travel with Abraham's servant. Laban gives them water to wash their feet, and they eat, stay the night and return with the servant.

aliases: the daughters of the men of the city
entities.summary_bio: The women of the city who come out to the well in the evening to draw water. The servant waits among them for the one who will answer his prayer.

entities.etymology_meaning: The city named after Abraham's brother Nahor, where his household settled.
entities.summary_bio: The city in Aram-naharaim where Nahor's family lives and where Bethuel's house stands. The servant stops at its well on arriving in the evening.

entities.etymology_meaning: 'Beit' means house, here the household of Rebekah's father.
entities.summary_bio: The home of Bethuel, Laban and Rebekah in Nahor's city. Laban brings the servant here, where he tells his errand, the family consents, and Rebekah leaves with him.

entities.etymology_meaning: Aram-naharayim means 'Aram of the two rivers', the land between the Euphrates and its tributary or the Tigris.
entities.summary_bio: The northern region where Nahor's family lives. Abraham's servant travels there from Canaan to find a wife for Isaac from among Abraham's kin.

aliases: the tent of Sarah his mother
entities.summary_bio: The tent that had belonged to Sarah, Isaac's mother. Isaac brings Rebekah into it and marries her.

entities.etymology_meaning: 'Be'er ha-mayim' means well of water; v.13 calls it 'ayin', a spring.
entities.summary_bio: A well outside the city where the women come at evening to draw water. Here the servant prays, meets Rebekah, and gives her the first gifts.

entities.etymology_meaning: Unnamed; the Hebrew 'eved' means servant or slave. Later Jewish tradition calls him Eliezer, but the chapter does not.
entities.summary_bio: The senior servant of Abraham's household, who rules over all that Abraham owns. Abraham makes him swear to fetch a wife for Isaac from his own kindred; he travels to Nahor's city with ten camels, prays at the well, and brings Rebekah home.

entities.etymology_meaning: Unnamed; 'em' means mother. Her name is not given in Genesis; Milcah is the wife of Nahor, Bethuel's mother, not Rebekah's.
entities.summary_bio: The mother of Rebekah and Laban, wife of Bethuel. Rebekah runs to her house with the news, and she joins Laban in asking for ten days' delay and in receiving the servant's gifts.

entities.etymology_meaning: Unnamed here; Hebrew 'meneqet' means a wet-nurse or a woman who raised a child.
entities.summary_bio: The woman who nursed and raised Rebekah. She goes with her when her family sends her off to marry Isaac (24:59).

components.evidence_explanation: 24:1 says Abraham was old and well advanced in days.
24:1 says the LORD had blessed Abraham in everything.
24:9 shows the servant swearing to Abraham with his hand under his thigh.

components.label_value: Refusing food until his errand is told
components.evidence_explanation: 24:33 has him say he will not eat until he has spoken his words; he eats in 24:54.
24:2 calls him the eldest servant of his house who rules over all that Abraham has.
24:53 has the servant give the silver, gold and garments to Rebekah.
24:22 shows the bracelets put on her hands.
24:22 and 24:30 show the ring on Rebekah.
24:67 says Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.
24:62 says Isaac was living in the land of the Negeb.
24:28 has her run to her mother's house and 24:61 shows her leaving it.
24:67 says Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother.
24:16 says she was a virgin and no man had known her.
24:51 has Laban and Bethuel say she may be wife to Isaac, and 24:53 has the gifts given.
24:67 says Isaac took Rebekah and she became his wife.

systems.name: Family blessing of a departing bride
systems.ancient_near_east_context: When a bride left her family's house for her husband's, her kin sent her off with words of good wishes. Genesis 24:60 is the clearest case in the Bible; it is spoken by her brother and mother, not by a father at the end of his life as in the patriarchal blessings (Gen 27).
rules_and_mechanics: Her kin speak the blessing at the moment of sending her off (24:59-60).
It is addressed to the bride herself, who is called 'our sister'.
It wishes her fertility: that she become thousands of myriads.
It wishes her offspring victory: that they possess the gate of those who hate them.

systems.name: Veiling of the bride
systems.ancient_near_east_context: Genesis attests this one case of a woman covering herself with the tsa'if (veil) on first seeing her future husband. Veils carried other meanings elsewhere: in Gen 38:14-15 Tamar covers herself and Judah takes her for a prostitute, so a veil did not by itself signal a marriage.
rules_and_mechanics: The bride covers herself with the veil (tsa'if) when she first sees the groom (24:65).

systems.name: Bridewealth and betrothal gifts
systems.ancient_near_east_context: Marriage in the ancient Near East involved payment (Hebrew mohar) or gifts from the groom's family to the bride's family, and often jewellery and clothing for the bride herself.
rules_and_mechanics: Gifts come from the groom's family, here through the envoy.
Part goes to the bride (jewellery, clothing) and part to her brother and mother.
A first gift can be given before the family agrees, as a token.
Receiving the gifts signals that the betrothal is accepted.

systems.name: Arranged marriage negotiated with the bride's family
systems.ancient_near_east_context: In the ancient Near East a marriage was normally arranged between the families, with the father or brothers of the bride giving consent and the groom's side paying gifts. A trusted envoy could act for an absent groom, and the bride's own agreement was sometimes asked.
rules_and_mechanics: The groom's family sends an envoy rather than the groom himself.
The envoy states his errand and his master's credentials before eating.
The bride's father and brother give or withhold consent.
Gifts are given to the bride and her family when consent is given.
The bride may be asked whether she will go.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The servant brings out silver and gold articles and garments for Rebekah, and precious things for her brother and mother.
system_instances.significance_note: The gifts seal the betrothal and honor the family.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Her family blesses Rebekah that she may become thousands of myriads and that her offspring possess the gate of their enemies.
system_instances.significance_note: The blessing echoes God's promise to Abraham (22:17) and marks Rebekah's entry into the covenant line.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Laban and Bethuel say the matter comes from the LORD and that Rebekah may go and be Isaac's wife.
system_instances.significance_note: The bride's family accepts the proposal and ties it to the LORD's will.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The servant praises the LORD who has not left off his loyalty and faithfulness to Abraham and has led him to his master's kin.
system_instances.significance_note: Gives the narrative's own reading of the events: God's providence, not luck, brings Rebekah to the well.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Isaac brings Rebekah into his mother Sarah's tent, takes her as wife, and loves her.
system_instances.significance_note: Completes the servant's errand and carries the covenant line forward; Isaac is comforted after Sarah's death.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Laban gives the servant room in the house, straw and fodder for the camels, and water to wash the feet of the servant and his men.
system_instances.significance_note: The welcome shows the kinship ties the servant came to renew.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The servant tells the family who his master is, what Abraham charged him with, how Rebekah answered his prayer, and asks if they will deal loyally with Abraham.
system_instances.significance_note: He presents the match as God's doing and asks them to agree.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Her family asks Rebekah whether she will go with the man; she says 'I will go'.
system_instances.significance_note: Rebekah's own consent decides the matter after her family had asked her to delay.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Seeing Isaac, Rebekah gets down from the camel and covers herself with her veil.
system_instances.significance_note: Shows her as a bride meeting her husband for the first time.

system_instances.outcome_summary: After the camels drink, the servant gives Rebekah a gold ring and two gold bracelets.
system_instances.significance_note: The gifts show the family what kind of household the servant serves, and Laban's reaction to them draws him to the well.

system_instances.outcome_summary: On hearing their answer the servant bows to the ground before the LORD.
system_instances.significance_note: Marks the second time he answers God's guidance with worship.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The servant asks that the young woman who offers him a drink and waters his camels be the one chosen for Isaac.
system_instances.significance_note: He lets Rebekah's kindness prove God's choice instead of picking her himself.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The servant puts his hand under Abraham's thigh and swears by the LORD not to take a wife for Isaac from the Canaanites, but from Abraham's own kindred.
system_instances.significance_note: The oath binds the servant to Abraham's covenant aim: Isaac must marry within the family and must not go back to the old homeland.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The servant bows low and worships the LORD at the well.
system_instances.significance_note: He treats the meeting as God's answer before he knows the family's response.

edges.description: Abraham charges his servant to go to his own land and kindred and take a wife for Isaac.
Bethuel joins Laban in saying the matter comes from the LORD.
Isaac loved Rebekah, and was comforted after his mother's death.
Isaac takes Rebekah into his mother's tent and she becomes his wife.
Her family blesses Rebekah as they send her off.
Laban says the matter comes from the LORD and gives his consent.
Laban invites the servant into the house and says he has prepared room.
Asked if she will go with the man, Rebekah answers 'I will go'.
Rebekah runs to her mother's house and tells what happened.
Rebekah draws water until all the camels have drunk.
Rebekah lowers her jar and gives the servant a drink.
The servant says 'Blessed be the LORD, God of my master Abraham'.
The servant gives precious things to Laban and Rebekah's mother.
The servant gives Rebekah silver and gold articles and garments.
The servant gives Rebekah a gold ring and two gold bracelets.
The servant asks the LORD to show kindness to Abraham by granting success at the well.
The servant asks Laban and Bethuel to say whether they will deal loyally with Abraham.
The servant tells Isaac everything he has done.
The servant puts his hand under Abraham's thigh and swears to carry out the charge.
The LORD led the servant on the way to the house of his master's kin.
